Application Materials.content:
**Applicants should scan and submit the following documents to the Online Application System for evaluation of their applications:**
- Identity documents (e.g. Identity card*, passport or other travel document)
- Official Transcript (for academic qualifications of undergraduate and/or postgraduate studies):
- An official final transcript for a completed programme
- The latest transcript if the programme is not yet completed
- An official English-translated copy must be attached if the transcript is not in English. The interpretation of grades (in English) is also required.
- Degree Certificate/Graduation Certificate/Proof of Study (as appropriate)
- Verification proof by third-party authorities (for a completed programme):
- Online Verification Report of Higher Education Degree Certificate (中國高等教育學位在綫驗証報告), both Chinese and English versions, issued by the CHSI (中國高等教育學生信息網) for qualification(s) awarded by universities in the Chinese Mainland
- Online Query of Overseas Credentials Evaluation Reports 國(境)外學歷學位認証書 issued by the Chinese Service Center for Scholarly Exchange (CSCSE) (教育部留學服務中心) (applicable to applicants from the Chinese Mainland with qualifications awarded by overseas universities)
- Proof of English language proficiency, e.g. IETLS, TOEFL, CET-6 Score Report (applicable to applicants whose degree, or exceptionally, an alternative qualification deemed equivalent, was not awarded by a tertiary institution where English was used as the MOI for the degree programme)
- Personal statement
- Reference letters (if any)
*Do not upload copy of HKID. Local students will be required to present HKID for verification upon registration.*
Applicants may be required to submit a Report for Qualifications Assessment issued by the Hong Kong Council for Accreditation of Academic & Vocational Qualifications (HKCAAVQ) to support their application.

Interview Requirements.content: Shortlisted candidates may be required to attend an interview conducted by the Admission Panel.

Academic Requirements.content:
This programme values **interdisciplinary perspectives**, especially where data analytics intersects with industrial applications, business processes, or decision-making. For a Master's Degree, an applicant shall normally:
- hold a **relevant bachelor's degree** awarded by a tertiary education institution recognised for this purpose by the University; or
- have obtained an equivalent qualification; or
- have provided satisfactory evidence of academic and professional attainment.
A relevant bachelor's degree includes, but is not limited to:
- **Engineering** (e.g., mechanical, electrical, energy, transportation, logistics, and healthcare)
- **Computer Science** / **Information Technology**
- **Statistics** / **Mathematics** / **Applied Mathematics**
- **Data Science** / **Artificial Intelligence**
- **Business Analytics** / **Management Science**
- **Operations Research** / **Supply Chain Management**
- **Economics** / **Finance**
- **Information Systems** / **Industrial Management**
Applicants from **other disciplines** with strong quantitative, analytical, or technical backgrounds are also encouraged to apply.
Applicants with no or limited background in computer science or statistics will be required to complete non-credit-bearing pre-entry course(s):
- Introduction to Computing
- Statistics

Program Overview.content:
**Uniqueness of the Programme**
- **Becoming Competitive Candidates in the Job Market:** Nurturing graduates with expertise spanning **embodied artificial intelligence**, **data science**, **automatic control**, **industrial engineering**, **artificial intelligence**, **business analytics**, and more.
- **Forward-looking Vision:** Among the first in Hong Kong to integrate data science and industrial analytics, this programme will equip students with knowledge in industrial data analytics, data visualization, artificial intelligence, statistics, operations management, control systems, and the Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT).
- **Data Analytics with Purpose:** Fostering students to gain an in-depth understanding of the data generation process, to effectively communicate with various stakeholders, and conduct data analytics guided by two key questions: 1. Where do data come from? 2. Where will data analytics be applied?
- **Engaging with Real-World Industries:** Guiding students to address real-world industrial challenges systematically and comprehensively in various industries such as manufacturing, energy, transportation, logistics, and healthcare through industrial data analytics project.
[Download Programme Brochure](https://www.ln.edu.hk/sds/dids/ida/programme-overview/programme-leaflet)

Curriculum.content:
The total credit requirement for the MScIDA programme is **30 credits**, consisting of five required courses and five elective courses. These courses can have different combinations of lectures, laboratory sessions, tutorials, and/or seminars. Although the normal duration for the MScIDA programme is **one year of full-time study**, students may extend this up to a maximum duration of three years, subject to the approval of the Programme Director and the Person-in-Charge of the Division.
| Programme Curriculum | |
| --- | --- |
| **Required Courses (15 Credits)** | |
| 1. Strategic Visual Data Analytics | 3 credits |
| 2. Programming with Generative Artificial Intelligence | 3 credits |
| 3. Smart Connectivity and Fusion | 3 credits |
| 4. Intelligent Control and AI-Driven Analytics | 3 credits |
| 5. Industrial Data Analytics Project | 3 credits |
| **Elective Courses** | **Any five courses (15 credits) from the provided list** |
| 1. Introduction to Embodied Intelligence | 3 credits |
| 2. Introduction to Digital Twin | 3 credits |
| 3. Introduction to Large Language Models | 3 credits |
| 4. Practical Application of Deep Learning | 3 credits |
| 5. Big Data Analytics | 3 credits |
| 6. Healthcare Analytics | 3 credits |
| 7. Blockchain-driven Applications | 3 credits |
| 8. Smart Logistics | 3 credits |
| 9. Operational Research | 3 credits |
| 10. Urban Data Science and Analytics | 3 credits |
*The offering of elective courses is subject to sufficient demand and faculty availability.*
Applicants with no or limited background in computer science or statistics will be required to complete non-credit-bearing pre-entry course(s):
- Introduction to Computing
- Statistics
For graduation, students are required to complete a total of **10 courses of 30 credits**, as specified in the programme curriculum, including five required courses and five elective courses.

Cost of Attendance.content:
**Living Expenses**
**First Month** It is recommended that students prepare a budget of HK$6,200 - $7,500 to cover their first month's expenses.
**Estimated Monthly Expenses** The estimated monthly expenses may vary depending on individual lifestyle and spending habits. The following table is provided for general reference only:
| Item | Approx. expenses per month (HKD) |
| --- | --- |
| Meals (on campus) | HK$4,500 - $5,000 |
| Entertainment | HK$600 - $700 |
| Transportation (local) | HK$600 - $800 |
| Miscellaneous | HK$500 - $1,000 |
| **Total** | **HK$6,200 - $7,500** |

Financial Aid.content:
**Scholarships**
Scholarships may be awarded to outstanding students on the basis of academic merit. All students admitted to the programme will automatically be the candidates for the scholarships; no application is required.

Multiple Applications.content: You are required to submit separate applications if you wish to make multiple applications for different programmes of our School. Please also note that multiple application fees should be paid. Your chance of success will not be affected. However, applicants are not encouraged to switch to another programme once an admission offer has been accepted. Please be aware that the deposit fee will not be refunded if you decide to switch to another programme.

Deferral Admission Policy.content:
An applicant who has been offered admission to an approved programme of study is required to register with the Programme Office on a specified date. An applicant who fails to pay the prescribed fees or register on the relevant specified dates is considered as having forgone his/her place offered by the University.
A student who for special reasons seeks permission for deferment of his/her registration may apply in writing to the Programme Director **at least one week before the specified date for registration**. A fee for late registration will be charged by the Programme Office.

Conditional Admission Policy.content: You do not need to graduate from your bachelor's degree for master's degree applications at the time of application. However, you must obtain the respective degree **on or before August 15 of your admission year**.
